stories.title: Idle log-noise + sync-cadence hygiene (F-077 + F-078 + F-058, verify-first)
stories.completionNotes: Committed 18c5574. VERIFY-FIRST performed via CODE INSPECTION (no live-Pi/SSH access in headless Windows dev + BENCH-ONLY sprint) -- established what prior work already fixed and root-caused the residual idle sources from code, changing code ONLY where code evidence showed a real un-fixed gap. Findings: (a) connection_log outage churn already ~99%-deduped by US-340b; (b) sync cadence already engine-aware via US-298/299 SyncCadenceController (60s IDLE heartbeat, B-053). TWO residual code-confirmed idle sources fixed: [F-078 sync_history] server postSync() creates a sync_history row on EVERY POST (sync.py:1115, before any payload check), and pushDriveCounter() POSTed unconditionally whenever last_drive_id>0 -- so each 60s engine-off heartbeat wrote 1 server sync_history row (~1/min, matches the observed ~1.5/min). pushDelta already skips the POST when zero delta rows (EMPTY, no network), so the counter push was the sole idle POST. FIX: pushDriveCounter now gates the POST on an unchanged-value process-local high-water mark (self._lastPushedDriveCounter), advanced ONLY on a SUCCESSFUL push (a FAILED push stays re-sendable next tick); forcePush passes force=True to bypass (power-down flush must always deliver, per the method's own 'forcePush is the explicit bypass point' docstring). Server upsert is monotonic GREATEST() so skipping unchanged re-pushes loses nothing; a real drive-start advance still delivers within one tick (identical delivery latency to pre-fix -- only the redundant re-pushes are removed), preserving US-413's 'server counter tracks the Pi' guarantee. NO server change needed (a POST legitimately writes a sync_history row; the fix is to stop the idle POSTs). [F-077/F-058 connection_log] ecu_silent_wait was NOT in the US-340b repeat-suppressed set, so engine-off-but-adapter-reachable logged one ecu_silent_wait per reduced-cadence poll (a 24/7 idle-growth source), and worse it was treated as a state-change so it also CLEARED the dedup tracker each poll. FIX: added EVENT_ECU_SILENT_WAIT to _REPEAT_SUPPRESSED_EVENTS -- repeats within an engine-off window collapse to one row; first occurrence per window + real state changes (reconnect_success on engine crank, disconnect) still log/clear the tracker (does NOT suppress real events, per AC). TDD: 4 new idle-gate tests + 2 new ecu_silent dedup tests (confirmed RED then GREEN). Ran SYNCHRONOUSLY: pi/sync + connection-log + orchestrator + diagnostics + bt-resilience + reconnect = 169 pass; orchestrator + obdii + server sync (test_sync, test_drive_counter_sync) = 742 pass, 1 skip; ruff clean on all 4 touched files. DEFERRED TO PM BENCH WINDOW (BENCH-ONLY validationMethod): the live idle-soak re-query -- confirm on the deployed Pi/server that connection_log + sync_history idle growth is materially reduced after deploy (validationCriteria). Wiring-path tests unaffected (they mock pushDriveCounter, asserting the orchestrator still calls it each tick; the gate lives inside the method). Scope-fenced: did NOT touch the SyncCadenceController cadence values, no_new_drives drain gate (explicitly warned against), or the server sync_history writer.

stories.title: Pi post-reboot clock-drift guard (F-080, code angle; verify-first)
stories.completionNotes: Committed e622db2. VERIFY-FIRST discharged via CODE INSPECTION (no live-Pi/SSH in headless Windows dev; BENCH-ONLY sprint) -- same deferral shape as US-417/US-418. The 'if still drifting' guard branch was built (the honest-instrument path is the durable fix regardless of the live clock's current state; the RTC/timesyncd ordering fix stays ops/AI-1). Implementation follows the SSOT design directive: src/pi/diagnostics/clock_sync.py is the single authoritative provider of the 'is this boot timestamp trustworthy?' fact; boot-log writers apply its verdict as policy (they do NOT each acquire their own clock signal). Two combined signals: (a) sanity FLOOR -- subprocess-free lexical ISO-8601 compare vs CLOCK_SANITY_FLOOR_ISO='2025-01-01T00:00:00Z' (no genuine Eclipse telemetry predates the project; a pre-floor wall clock is a definitive dead-RTC epoch/build-date reset -> flag unconditionally, floor WINS even if NTP later reads synced); (b) best-effort timedatectl NTPSynchronized probe -- tri-state True/False/None, an UNREACHABLE probe returns None and falls back to the floor alone so a non-systemd/dev box is never painted suspect (no false-positive flood). classifyClockQuality is pure/total (never raises, never spawns) -- the floor-only seam power_log uses (write-latency-sensitive, high volume); assessClockQuality (probe+classify) is the once-per-boot startup_log seam. Wiring: startup_log writer (boot_progress._writeStartupLogRow, threaded through arm()) stamps data_quality via assessClockQuality (full NTP probe, paid once/boot); all 5 power_log writers (logPowerReading/Transition/SavingEvent/ShutdownStage) stamp via floor-only classifyClockQuality default so the durability-critical power-down race adds ZERO NTP-probe latency. data_quality TEXT column added to power_log + startup_log schema (SCHEMA_POWER_LOG/SCHEMA_STARTUP_LOG) + idempotent PRAGMA-guarded ALTER migrations (ensurePowerLogDataQuality wired into ObdDatabase.initialize; ensureStartupLogDataQuality wired into the standalone boot-log write path) -- nullable, legacy rows stay NULL=unassessed. WIRE-STRIP (mandatory, not scope creep): data_quality is a Pi-LOCAL forensic flag; the server PowerLog/StartupLog models have NO data_quality column (verified models.py:742/787 -- server data_quality lives only on server-authored drive_summary/drive_statistics), so an un-stripped column would crash the server's SQLAlchemy bulk insert on the US-412/US-417 sync paths. Added 'data_quality' to sync_log._WIRE_STRIPPED_COLUMNS (alongside _sync_modified_at); applied in BOTH getDeltaRows (power_log delta path) and getSnapshotRows (startup_log snapshot path). Global strip is safe: power_log + startup_log are the ONLY Pi tables carrying data_quality (grepped src/pi -- realtime_data uses data_source; drive_summary data_quality is server-only), so the strip is a harmless no-op for every other syncing table. TDD: 38 US-419 tests (test_clock_sync classifier/probe/assessor incl. pre-NTP-sync-flags + garbage-does-not-crash + None-timestamp; test_startup_log_clock_quality writer wiring + legacy backfill; test_power_log_clock_quality all 4 writers + default-provider-sane-is-full; test_sync_data_quality_strip delta+snapshot wire-strip). VERIFICATION (synchronous): pytest 38 US-419-targeted = all pass; sync-path regression (tests/pi/data + tests/pi/sync + tests/common/sync + tests/server/test_power_log_sync + test_startup_log_sync + test_sync) = exit 0, no failures (~437 tests, confirms the wire-strip broke no sync path); ruff clean on all 11 touched files. NOTE: this uncommitted work was built by a prior session that stalled pre-commit (headless async-wait, the recurring US-416 pattern); Rex re-verified it SYNCHRONOUSLY end-to-end and committed. DEFERRED TO PM BENCH: the live-Pi re-query (timedatectl/hwclock/power_log timestamps) + a real pre-NTP-sync-boot IRL observation -- validationCriteria (BENCH-ONLY sprint).

stories.title: LTFT multi-drive trend card (F-096, carousel)
stories.completionNotes: Committed a42c76a. New carousel LTFT Trend card (F-096) built to the established SSOT / pure-consumer carousel pattern (mirrors US-400/401/406): a Python emitter is the single authoritative provider that CLASSIFIES the drift; the JS card only maps the verdict -> colour, it never classifies. (1) src/pi/splash/ltft_trend_emitter.py -- LTFT_PID='LONG_FUEL_TRIM_1' (the single 4G63 bank; bank 2 unlogged); readLtftTrend() aggregates per-drive avg/min/max over realtime_data grouped by drive_id, OLDEST->NEWEST, WHERE data_source='real' AND drive_id IS NOT NULL (fixture/replay/sim -- and the future US-424 foreign marker -- can never enter the tune trend; NULL-drive noise excluded); LEFT JOIN drive_summary for the axis ts (NULL honestly when a drive has trims but no summary). classifyLtftDrift(): |LTFT|<=5 ok, <=10 amber, >10 down -- thresholds GROUNDED in offices/tuner/cards/safe-range-fuel-trims.md (normal +/-5, danger >+/-10) + the AC. buildLtftTrendState() is pure: per-drive levels + a headline verdict + trend direction (migrating toward 0 = improving vs worsening, TREND_EPSILON_PCT=0.5 dead-band). HONEST-INSTRUMENT: below MIN_DRIVES_FOR_TREND=2 the headline level is FORCED to 'insufficient' -- a single in-band reading can never masquerade as a healthy green. makeLtftTrendEmitter() = best-effort atomic writer (ensureStatesDir+writeStateAtomic, C-5), reader injected as a zero-arg seam, NEVER raises. (2) carousel.js: ltftTrendView() pure builder + renderLtftTrendCard() DOM (multi-drive bar row, each bar coloured by its OWN drift level so a >+/-10% drive is visibly not-green) + tick() dispatch on data-state='ltft-trend' + api exports (ltftTrendView/fmtLtftPct). Defense-in-depth: the view ALSO forces 'insufficient' when sufficient!==true (a mislabeled state can't paint green -- same re-derive discipline as clearButtonView). (3) dashboard.html: 4th card slot data-state='ltft-trend'. (4) dashboard.css: .ltft-bars/.ltft-bar[data-level] (ok/amber/down) + muted .tile[data-level='insufficient']. (5) Tests: tests/pi/splash/test_ltft_trend_emitter.py (19 tests -- classifier boundaries, reader real-only+NULL-drive filter + oldest-first + driveLimit + LEFT-join-ts-null + aggregation, insufficient-never-green, empty, improving/worsening/stable, best-effort never-raise on reader+write failure) + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py US-420 node render-logic (_US420_NODE_SCRIPT: null->null, healthy->ok+points, drift>10->down distinct, insufficient->never-ok, mislabeled sufficient:false stays insufficient, fmtLtftPct signed 2dp) + HTML slot + CSS asserts; grew the S-1 card-count lock-down 3->4 (registering a card legitimately adds one slot). VERIFICATION (synchronous): pytest tests/pi/splash + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py + tests/deploy/test_splash_kit.py = all pass (1 expected skip); US-420 node test confirmed RUN not skipped (node on PATH, ~8s); ruff clean on all 3 touched Python files; node --check carousel.js clean (via test_carouselJs_passesNodeSyntaxCheck_s1). SCOPE: emitter+reader+card+tests only -- runtime wiring (calling emit() post-drive) is owner/deploy-side and deferred, EXACTLY matching the sibling emitters (grep confirms makeBatteryHealthEmitter/makeDtcEmitter/makeSystemStatusEmitter have NO src call site either). DEFERRED TO PM BENCH (BENCH-ONLY sprint): the on-Pi render against live multi-drive LTFT + the OSOYOO swipe drill (validationCriteria is fixture/DOM-satisfied off-Pi; live IRL is the bench gate).
